thread.title: Stock Market News: Dow Jones Plunges 464 Points; Time To Buy Gold? | Investor's Business Daily

author: KEN SHREVE
title: Stock Market News: Dow Jones Plunges 464 Points; Time To Buy Gold? | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The bulls took another beating in the stock market today as Wall Street focused on plunging oil prices and the possibility of a government shutdown. In stock market news today , gold stocks outperformed, while Dow Jones component Apple ( AAPL ) fell 2% on more negative analyst commentary .
X The Nasdaq composite lost 1.6% and officially fell into bear market territory by falling more than 20% from its recent high. It also undercut its February intraday low of 6630. Meanwhile, selling in small caps continued. The Russell 2000 lost more than 1.7%. It's getting to close to its last breakout area, in November 2016, fueled by the presidential election results.
The Dow Jones industrial average fell 679 points, or 2.9% intraday, before ending with a loss of 2%. The S&P 500 dropped 1.6%.
As the stock market grapples with the economic outlook for 2019, a sharp drop in oil prices, and the path of interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, the threat of a federal government shutdown fueled more negative sentiment Thursday.
The Cboe Volatility Index, or the VIX, extended its winning streak to five sessions Thursday, jumping 10% to 28.21. It broke out over a recent high of 28.84 before backing off.
Dow component Walgreens Boots Alliance ( WBA ) got slammed on earnings , down 5%, despite pledging "transformational" cost cuts. It's trading near its 200-day moving average, a longer-term support level.
Crude oil continued its descent. U.S. crude oil futures settled at $45.88 a barrel, down 4.8% to a 17-month low. It's down more than 10% for the week.
Stock Market News: Gold Rallies SPDR Gold Shares ( GLD ) showed noteworthy action. After getting resistance at the 200-day moving average Wednesday, the exchanged traded fund jumped above the line with conviction Thursday, rising 1.5%.
Gold stocks were generally strong amid weakness in the U.S. dollar. IBD's gold miner group was by far the day's top performer, up around 5%. Inside the IBD 50 , Kirkland Gold ( KL ) rebounded nearly 4% after Wednesday's 5% haircut. The gold miner, highlighted last week in the IBD Stock Spotlight column , is back near highs as it sits comfortably above a 23.96 buy point .
In other stock market news, marijuana stock Tilray ( TLRY ) jumped 10% after it announced a partnership with Anheuser-Busch InBev ( BUD ) to research cannabis-based drinks.
